versions.python_requirements_txt:
# Pinned exact versions. Only the fast-tokenizer library and the Hub
# download client are required; no torch/tensorflow/flax (no model
# weights are loaded in this spike, only tokenizer.json files).
huggingface_hub==1.30.0
tokenizers==0.23.2

# Optional cross-check only (see scripts/cross_check_transformers.py):
# confirms transformers' AutoTokenizer wrapper applies the same
# normalization as loading tokenizer.json directly with `tokenizers`.
# transformers does not require torch to load a tokenizer, only to load
# model weights, so this stays torch-free.
transformers==5.16.1

bert-base-chinese.note: WordPiece, ~21k zh-focused vocab. Resolves to google-bert/bert-base-chinese.

distilbert-base-multilingual-cased.note: Distilled mBERT, shares mBERT's WordPiece vocab.

ckiplab-bert-tiny-chinese-ner.note: Academia Sinica CKIP NER fine-tune. Ships tokenizer_config.json / special_tokens_map.json / vocab.txt but no tokenizer.json (slow tokenizer only). Its tokenizer_config.json has name_or_path='bert-base-chinese'. This script verifies vocab.txt is byte-identical to bert-base-chinese's before reusing that tokenizer.json here.

metadata.offsets_api_finding: transformers.js (@huggingface/transformers 4.2.0) does not expose character offsets anywhere in its public API. Empirically, calling tokenizer(text, {return_offsets_mapping: true}) returns the same {input_ids, attention_mask} shape as without the option -- no offset_mapping key ever appears. `grep -rn 'return_offsets_mapping|offset_mapping' src/` over the installed package (v4.2.0) returns zero matches: the option is not merely ignored, it is not implemented anywhere in the library. Its own token-classification pipeline has the same gap: src/pipelines/token-classification.js pushes {entity, score, index, word} per token with a literal source comment `// TODO: Add support for start and end` and never sets them, so even the NER pipeline example in that file's own docstring returns no span. Only tokenizer.tokenize(text) [content token strings, no specials] and tokenizer.encode(text) [input_ids, specials included] are available.
